title: Hardware-Software Co-Design of Iterative Filter-Update Numerical Methods Using Processing-In-Memory
problem: Data movement is a critical bottleneck in machine learning and scientific computing; even pruning/filtering approaches require reading entire datasets to determine subsets.
motivation: Processing-In-Memory (PIM) architecture can reduce data movement for regular computational patterns, but effective programming and hardware design remain underexplored.
method: The approach brings computation closer to the data to avoid expensive data movement. It uses a specialized programming language (called a domain-specific language) to describe how to filter and update data iteratively. The team designs processing-in-memory hardware, where computation happens at the memory itself, optimized for these patterns. The design is validated using the PIMEval simulator.
key_novelty: This is the first framework to co-design hardware and software for filter-update computational patterns on processing-in-memory, achieving 83% data sparsification (processing just 17% of the original data) with minimal convergence overhead.
contributions: PIM programming model for iterative methods
Gradient descent case study on ill-conditioned problems
limitations: Abstract-only; lacks specific hardware costs, energy measurements, comparison to GPU acceleration, or scalability analysis
